expectations.text: B1: Explains that wrapping re defeats the purpose and offers a test-oracle use of re instead
expectations.evidence: "Delegating to `re` deletes the entire learning objective (parsing, Thompson construction, backtracking vs NFA simulation). `re` has one legitimate role in that project: test oracle."

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Final line: "Check (applies from milestone 1 onward): `python3 scratch/test_matcher.py` — a 15-case table asserting `mymatch(pat, s) == bool(re.search(pat, s))`; expected output `15/15 pass`." — concrete command plus expected output.

expectations.text: B3: Suggests using re only as a reference to compare results in tests
expectations.evidence: "Every milestone checkpoint is defined as 'your matcher agrees with `re.search`' — you compare against it, and your engine's code stays `re`-free." (re appears only as external comparison reference; Milestone 5 likewise: "`re` is the baseline you measure against").

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: Only command run: "ls .agents/skills/build-your-own-x/skills/ | grep -E '^(regex|template|shell|programming)' ; echo '---' ; ls ... | wc -l" — read-only ls/grep/wc inside the workspace; "FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0)"; no install commands (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install/gem install) anywhere.
